2026
Directorate-General
for International Partnerships

PART 1. Introduction
In a rapidly evolving and increasingly complex international landscape, marked by intensifying
geopolitical and geoeconomic competition, multiplying conflicts, and pressing global challenges,
the Directorate-General for International Partnerships (DG INTPA) delivers on its mandate by
establishing mutually beneficial partnerships based on intersecting interests. It promotes
sustainable investments across the globe under the Global Gateway strategy, engages with
countries in highly fragile and complex settings, contributes to an effective EU migration policy
within comprehensive partnerships and to implementing global commitments, notably the
United Nations (UN) 2030 Agenda, the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the Paris
Agreement.
Strategic planning and programming is the cornerstone of the
management framework. The -2029 translates the
political priorities set in the Political Guidelines of President von der Leyen into general
objectives. This process ensures institutional coherence, enhances accountability, and aligns the
actions of all Commission services with the strategic vision of the mandate.
Within this framework, each Commission service has developed a strategic outlook for
2025-2029 in the 2025 Management Plan. This outlook defines a set of multiannual
objectives and indicators to measure progress towards their achievement. These will be used
for planning and reporting on performance throughout the period.
The 2026 management plan sets out what DG INTPA intends to deliver this year to
contribute to these multiannual objectives (part 2). It also describes how DG INTPA will
contribute to the common objective of building a modern and sustainable public administration
(part 3). The main outputs with their indicators and targets are presented in Annexes 1 and 2.
The chart below illustrates the performance framework for DG INTPA.

priorities in 2026

planned for 2026 will contribute to the achievement of the European Commission general
objective 6 - through the pursuit of
nine specific objectives.
Specific objective 6.1: Strategic partnerships at country, regional and global levels
are further strengthened through mutually beneficial investments in favour of
sustainable development
In 2026, DG INTPA will continue the rollout of Global Gateway
strategy to boosts investments in quality and sustainable infrastructure in partner countries to
create prosperity, decent jobs, while strengthening connections between the EU and its partners
across continents. It will also contribute to strengthening Global Gateway governance by
organising regular meetings of the Global Gateway Board, chaired by the Commissioner for
International Partnerships as per delegation from the President.
DG INTPA will actively implement and monitor the commitments of the European Union (EU) -
of the 7th AU-EU Summit (Angola, November
2025), notably through the Global Gateway Africa-Europe Investment Package and the
ongoing scale-up of key initiatives. DG INTPA will concentrate its efforts on several
transformative initiatives in Sub-Saharan Africa, including: (i) the Lobito corridor linking
Angola, Zambia, and the Democratic Republic of Congo; (ii) the Africa-Europe Green Energy
Initiative to advance on an energy transition that is fair, just and equitable; and (iii) the
Europe Initiative on Manufacturing and Access to Vaccines, Medicines and Health
in Rwanda, South Africa, Ghana, Nigeria and Senegal. The
implementation of the Samoa Agreement will advance with the convening of the remaining
constitutive meetings of the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States (OACPS)-EU
Ministerial Councils and Ambassadorial Committees, at foundation and regional protocol levels,
as well as the parliamentary level meetings.
In 2026, the EU will continue to strengthen its economic, social and political ties with the Latin
America and the Caribbean (LAC) region and the Overseas Countries and Territories (OCTs).
Building on the IV Community of Latin American and Caribbean States (CELAC) EU Summit
(Colombia, November 2025), joint efforts will focus on a green and digital transition and
tackling transnational organised crime.
To deliver the EU-LAC Global Gateway Investment Agenda, several major Global Gateway
flagship projects like the LAC regional electricity integration and the valorisation of Sargassum
for the Caribbean will be prioritised. Under the EU-LAC Digital Alliance, 2026 will mark the

4

roll-out of a new pillar to drive digital transformation of LAC, as part of the Global Gateway
strategy.
The importance of the partnership with the OCTs will be reaffirmed in 2026 at the OCTs-EU
Forum in Aruba and through regular tripartite meetings, strengthening links on strategic issues
(including critical raw materials (CRMs), particularly with Greenland). Cooperation with the OCTs,
including Greenland, will continue in sectors of common interest such as digital connectivity,
renewable energies, climate change and human development with a focus on strengthening
regional integration and mobilising private investment under the Global Gateway strategy.
Following the first ever EU-Central Asia Summit in April 2025, DG INTPA will focus on
delivering on the Team Europe EUR 12 billion Global Gateway Investment Package. This
package targets four key priority areas of EU cooperation with the region: (i) transport, in
particular the Trans-Caspian Transport Corridor; (ii) digital connectivity; (iii) CRMs, and (iv)
water, energy and climate change. In energy, for instance, progress is anticipated notably with
funding for the Rogun and Kambarata hydropower plants in Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan.
In the current geopolitical environment, marked by tensions in the Indo-Pacific region and
shifting global trends, DG INTPA remains committed to delivering on the Global Gateway
strategy in partner countries as well as working closely with like-minded countries to amplify its
impact in the region.
In South-East Asia, while preparing the EU-Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)
Commemorative Summit for the 50th anniversary of EU-ASEAN relations in 2027, DG INTPA
will continue its support nationally and regionally to the green, energy and digital transition,
sustainable connectivity, as well as to skills development and good governance. In particular,
DG INTPA will boost cooperation on energy connectivity through the ASEAN Power Grid and Just
Energy Transition Partnerships in Vietnam and Indonesia. In South Asia (2), DG INTPA will
continue to support energy transition and connectivity at regional level under the Global
Gateway flagship project Energy connectivity in South Asia promoting cross-border electricity
trade and energy connectivity at bilateral level. Following the visit of the College of
Commissioners in February 2025 and in line with the new Strategic EU-India Agenda adopted in
September 2025, cooperation with India will further deepen, with the EU-India Summit in
January 2026. The EU intends to position itself as a partner of reference to India, by increasing
policy dialogue, investments in critical areas of mutual interest, including around the India-
Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor, as well as by intensifying trilateral cooperation in
sectors and geographies where the EU and India can combine their expertise to support
sustainable development in partner countries.
During 2026, DG INTPA is expected to strengthen its efforts towards the development of
important Global Gateway infrastructure projects in the Pacific region, addressing remoteness
and fragility in the face of climate change. The priorities identified are digital and transport
connectivity, climate-resilient infrastructure in the fields of water and energy, blue economy
and oceans governance, and private sector development, notably in agricultural value chains.
(2) South Asia countries are Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Sri Lanka.

Specific objective 6.2: In line with the Global Gateway strategy, scale up with partner
countries mutually beneficial investments in secure, universal and meaningful
connectivity, data, space, trustworthy artificial intelligence, and other relevant
priorities for digital transformation
In line with the Global Gateway strategy and the new EU International Digital Strategy, DG
INTPA, in collaboration with EU Member States and the private sector, will consolidate and
expand investments in digital infrastructures across priority geographies and market segments
through an integrated EU tech business offer. It will do so notably through the EU-LAC
supercomputing network, the Blue Raman flagship project and the Digital Economy Package
launched in Mozambique. To do so, in 2026, DG INTPA will deepen existing partnerships and
broaden them in Asia-Pacific region, LAC, and Africa to scale up mutually beneficial
investments in secure and trusted digital infrastructure and emerging technologies such as
trustworthy artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, open-source European digital solutions for
public services and for easier cross-border business activities as well as space-based services
and applications. This will include other digital technologies, such as data centres and data
services from the European Space Programme, notably Copernicus, Galileo and European
Geostationary Navigation Overlay Service. Unlocking investments in the rollout of secure and
trusted 5G networks, expanding satellite connectivity, and further developing a secure network
of submarine and terrestrial cables will remain a priority. This will help bridge the global digital
divide and connect the EU with like-minded countries. To ensure high-impact projects, the EU
will rely on the new Global Gateway Investment Hub to channel relevant digital investment
proposals from the EU private sector. The Digital for Development Hub will also remain a key
platform to facilitate investments at scale and deliver a sustainable and human-centric digital
transformation globally.
Specific objective 6.3: In line with the Global Gateway strategy, to support partner
countries in their transition to low-carbon and resource efficient economies, by
promoting investments for sustainable energy, sustainable agri-food systems,
sustainable cities, water and green economy solutions to mitigate climate change
and biodiversity loss, and by enhancing their capacities to adapt to their impacts,
including via circular economy, sustainable management of natural resources and
mutually beneficial critical raw material (CRM) partnerships
In the framework of the Global Gateway strategy, DG INTPA will engage with partner countries
through Team Europe initiatives, supporting the implementation of the Paris Agreement and the
transition to low-carbon, resource-efficient, and competitive circular economies. It will also
integrate climate and environmental goals into EU-funded actions across all relevant sectors.
The scaling up of renewables in Africa will be achieved, notably under the Africa-Europe
Green Energy Initiative. Support to the energy transition and regional electricity integration
will be a priority in the Asia-Pacific, Sub-Saharan Africa and LAC regions. DG INTPA will support
cities in their response to climate challenges and will promote sustainable urban mobility in the
context of the Covenant for Mayors in Sub-Saharan Africa, inter alia through the Mobilise Your
City initiative. Investments will also be promoted in the water and sanitation sector, as well as
in nature-based solutions and circularity.
As part of Global Gateway strategy implementation, DG INTPA will support the development of
environmentally and socially sustainable, secure and resilient supply chains of Critical Raw
6

Materials (CRMs) to the EU. It will contribute to the implementation of strategic partnerships
external dimension requirements in relation to commitments under the CRM Act and other
relevant EU policies (i.e. RESourceEU plan). Following a Team Europe approach, and full
coherence with the functioning of the Global Gateway Investment Hub, special focus will be on
identifying concrete sustainable investment opportunities that are mutually beneficial and
suppliers.
DG INTPA will also implement initiatives to preserve biodiversity and sustainably exploit natural
resources, including through the NaturAfrica flagship project, the Great Green Wall, the
implementation of DG INTPA-driven actions under the Water Resilience Strategy and the Forest
Partnerships. DG INTPA will further promote sustainable practices like agroecology and
agroforestry for agricultural value chains that link local and regional suppliers with
international markets and enhance public and private investments, including through the Team
Europe Initiative on deforestation-free value chains and the Global Gateway flagship project on
Sustainable Cocoa (3).
Specific objective 6.4: In line with the Global Gateway strategy, promote worldwide
transport infrastructure investments including in urban nodes, that foster the
sustainable development of partner countries and reduce greenhouse gas emissions,
as well as enable the diversification of supply chains, seeking to increase EU
competitiveness
In line with the Global Gateway strategy, DG INTPA will aim to promote worldwide investments
in transport infrastructure, including in urban nodes, and to foster sustainable development in
partner countries, while reducing greenhouse gas emissions. DG INTPA will also support actions
on transport governance, transport and trade facilitation to accompany those investments.
These efforts will also target the diversification and decarbonisation of supply chains and the
enhancing of EU competitiveness, in line with the EU Competitiveness Compass and the Clean
Industrial Deal. Key initiatives like the Global Gateway Green Shipping Corridors, the
Sustainable Aviation Fuel flagship project and the aviation dialogues will target clean modes of
transport, and sustainable and resilient infrastructure (e.g. ports or roads). As part of the Global
Gateway strategy, DG INTPA will work towards integrating sustainable, productive and inclusive
cities in a wider concept of development corridors. By targeting collaborations across Asia-
Pacific region, LAC and Africa, DG INTPA will focus on promoting EU-led sustainable transport
technologies and standards, safe and efficient deployment of low-emission mobility solutions,
regulations and policies. A critical priority will be unlocking investments to develop resilient and
climate-friendly transport networks, based on the priority corridors approach and aimed, inter
alia, at providing secure and sustainable supply of CRMs lobal
Gateway Transport Support Mechanism, the Urban Development Technical Facility and new
collaborations with international or EU organisations will be pivotal to maximise collaborative
work between EU Member States and the private sector, financing entities and partner
countries to collectively scale up investments.
(3) The Global Gateway flagship initiative on Sustainable Cocoa already covered
started to operate in Guinea Conakry, Liberia, Nigeria and Sierra Leone in 2025.

Specific objective 6.5: In line with the Global Gateway strategy, human development
for all is improved with a special focus on the most vulnerable populations, through
interventions in health, education, and research and contributing to the overall aim
of reducing poverty
In 2026, DG INTPA will continue to ensure that the Global Gateway strategy delivers concrete
results in advancing human development, with a strong focus on health, education, skills,
research, and innovation.
Health will remain one of the priority areas of DG INTPA. In 2026, DG INTPA will roll out the
Global Health Resilience Initiative (4) in alignment with the Global Gateway strategy and the EU
Global Health strategy. DG INTPA will continue to advance the local manufacturing agenda as
an integral component of the Global Gateway strategy and broader aims of strengthening
health sovereignty and autonomy. Finally, it will reinforce the interlinkages between social
protection, gender equality and health, with increased emphasis on the care economy.
DG INTPA will continue to anchor skills as a crucial enabling dimension of Global
Gateway strategy. This will include aligning education and training systems with the needs of
priority value chains and fostering stronger links between skills development, business, and
investment to maximise the long-term impact of Global Gateway projects. In particular, DG
INTPA will continue embedding skills in the Global Gateway investments and sectors, including
through the Opportunity-driven Skills and Vocational education and training in Africa
programme and through public-private dialogue and sector exchanges. DG INTPA will also
continue advancing robust education and training systems in fragile settings.
In 2026, the EU Youth Action Plan in External Action will be evaluated. A new Global Youth
Sounding Board will be established to strengthen structured dialogue and ensure young
strategy and in the EU approach to fragile settings.
DG INTPA will continue to promote , including
through innovative financing and programming flagship initiatives. On the basis of the Gender
Action Plan (GAP) III evaluation, DG INTPA will launch the preparations of the post-2027 Gender
Action Plan (GAP IV), with a targeted stakeholder consultation in Spring 2026, presented in
conjunction with the adoption of the new Gender Equality strategy.
DG INTPA remains committed to ensuring that our interventions leave no one behind. As
part of this effort, investments will be promoted to support sustainable and inclusive water
access, sanitation and hygiene, notably in the most vulnerable areas, such as the Sahel or the
Democratic Republic of Congo. To ensure continued progress, DG INTPA will continue using a
range of tools to make our actions more inclusive, such as the Organisation of Economic
Cooperation and Development (OECD) Development Assistance Committee (DAC) Gender
Equality Policy Marker, the Disability Marker and the Inequality Marker (I-Marker).
In the area of culture, DG INTPA will continue to work on cultural and creative industries,
promoting skills, employment, and sustainable growth. Efforts will focus on strengthening EU

Africa cultural partnerships, and deepening collaboration with Team Europe to enhance the role
of culture in sustainable development.
Specific objective 6.6: In line with the Global Gateway strategy and its 360-degree
approach, enhance partner countries' business enabling environment for sustainable
and quality investments
DG INTPA will support mutually beneficial strategic investments in partner countries, with
emphasis, at micro and macro levels, on promoting an enabling environment for socially and
-based
approach.
DG INTPA will strengthen its work around private sector engagement and its participation in
the Global Gateway strategy implementation via the Global Gateway Investment Hub launched
at the Global Gateway Forum (9-10 October 2025). EU companies will be able to submit their
project proposals mostly through their Team National set-up (5). DG INTPA will support EU
delegations in the organisation of business fora and in private sector-led events facilitating
networking and deal-making between companies and partner countries. DG INTPA will work on
deepening its understanding of the employment impact of its investment programmes whilst
continuing to build capacity on decent work and corporate sustainability.
To scale up external investments aligned with EU priorities under the Global Gateway strategy
and ensure leverage for EU funding and mobilisation of private capital, European Fund for
Sustainable Development Plus (EFSD+) budgetary guarantees and blending will actively
support access to finance for public and private actors. DG INTPA will enhance its support for a
conducive investment climate in partner countries, targeting those where efforts to improve the
trade and investment environment will have the greatest impact and contribution to the
successful implementation of Global Gateway projects. This will apply to project proposals
under the Global Gateway Investment Hub.
DG INTPA will coordinate budget support to facilitate the creation of an enabling environment
for Global Gateway investments in partner countries with fragile and complex settings. In
addition, DG INTPA will provide support to economic governance, public finance management
and macro-fiscal reforms to strengthen economic resilience, mobilise domestic revenues,
reduce debt vulnerabilities, and ensure a more secure environment for private sector
investment decisions. To amplify impact, DG INTPA will coordinate strategic partnerships with
international financial institutions, such as the World Bank Group and the International
Monetary Fund, to promote EU priorities and further the Global Gateway agenda.
The Global Green Bond Initiative Fund is expected to start its operations to invest in green
bonds issued by low-and middle-income countries, while the Green Coupon Subsidy Facility
will be established to lower the cost of capital for eligible issuers under specific circumstances.
The Sustainable Finance Advisory Hub will fully deploy its technical assistance for green bonds
and expand the development of sustainable finance frameworks and taxonomies, including
through a global taxonomy mapper.
(5) Process at national level to bring all relevant actors together in view of Global Gateway strategy implementation.
9

DG INTPA will strengthen the systematic application of the -degree
approach, which comprises the six key principles (6) set out in the Global Gateway
Communication and the creation of an enabling environment for sustainable and quality
investments, promoting high social, environmental and governance standards, rule of law and
open government reforms as well as an inclusive and participatory approach with civil society
In this framework, DG INTPA intends
to continue using the Global Gateway Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) and Local Authorities
Advisory Platform to reinforce the dialogue with CSOs and local authorities, to consult them on
the implementation of Global Gateway flagship projects and to share information about the
360-degree approach.
DG INTPA will also support policies that make clean and green investments and technologies an
economically competitive choice, while continuing to mainstream sustainability across Global
Gateway actions. This will be done by investing in resilience through, amongst others, the
sustainable management of natural resources, the support to nature-based solutions, and the
development of holistic partnerships on forests and green corridors. Cities located along the
corridors will also be a key area of action where DG INTPA will boost investment and job
creation.
Specific objective 6.7: In line with the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum and the EU
commitments towards forcibly displaced people, all aspects of migration and forced
displacement governance are improved in key partner countries, with a focus on
reducing irregular migration towards the EU
While the number of irregular migrants coming to the EU is decreasing, the trend of increasing
numbers of migrants and forcibly displaced people at global level will demand continued EU
attention at both political and operational levels. With the new rules under the EU Pact on
Migration and Asylum being fully applicable from June 2026, it will be crucial to ensure
coherence between the implementation of its internal and external dimensions.
DG INTPA will continue to play a strong role in the concrete operationalisation of the
external dimension of the Pact. DG INTPA will step up its engagement and support to
establish mutually beneficial, strategic and comprehensive partnerships with key countries of
origin, transit and destination (including for forcibly displaced people) in a whole-of-route
approach, with a focus on key routes towards Europe.
DG INTPA support will contribute to incentivise partner countries to improve cooperation
on migration and forced displacement management, with attention to preventing irregular
migration, fighting smuggling of migrants and improving return, readmission and sustainable
reintegration. Increased opportunities for labour migration to the EU will also continue to be in
focus, including through the implementation of Talent Partnerships. Our global commitments to
assist migrants, refugees and other forcibly displaced populations and their host communities
will continue, with a focus on supporting inclusive policies and durable solutions.
In Sub-Saharan Africa, DG INTPA will continue to support the protection of migrants stranded
in the Sahel region, by assisting them with voluntary returns and providing reintegration

assistance to migrants returning to their country of origin. DG INTPA will continue strengthening
national systems, notably in four pilot countries: Senegal, Nigeria, Ghana, and Ivory Coast to
ensure better ownership of national authorities over the sustainable reintegration of their own
nationals. Fight against trafficking in human beings and smuggling of migrants will remain a
priority in Sub-Saharan Africa with actions targeting both Eastern and Western regions. Further
support to forced displacement situations in East and West Africa will back conducive policies
and plans in favour of durable solutions such as refugee inclusion, promoting out-of-camp
approaches, including national graduation strategies and strengthening basic services.
In 2026, DG INTPA will also focus on Afghan and Myanmar displacement crises and border
management initiatives in Asia and the Pacific. Support will include basic services, governance
improvements, and livelihoods for internally displaced persons (IDPs) in Myanmar, as well as
Myanmar people displaced in Thailand, and enhanced access to services, protection, education
and livelihoods for Afghan returnees, IDPs and host communities. Integrated Border
Management programmes will be launched in Pakistan and Bangladesh to promote human
rights-based border management and reduce irregular migration.
Further efforts will be needed to strengthen a Team Europe approach, pooling EU and its
political, diplomatic and financial tools in support of a joined-up EU
engagement with partner countries.
Specific objective 6.8: Good governance, resilience and peace are enhanced through
all available instruments in contexts affected by fragility or conflict and the risk of
conflict
DG INTPA will remain actively engaged in promoting good governance, resilience and
peace, recognising the intricate links between these aspects. The toolset for EU Conflict
Analysis, Conflict Early Warning System and Resilience Assessments will allow DG INTPA to
pursue more action-oriented analyses, incorporating the Global Gateway objectives and risks
into its actions and activities in fragile and conflict-affected contexts. By continuing to work
across the Humanitarian-Development-Peace nexus, DG INTPA will remain engaged and foster
a more comprehensive and sustainable response to the challenges posed by fragility and
conflict.
In 2026, DG INTPA will work with other Commission services, notably DG ECHO (7), on an EU
integrated approach to fragility (dedicated, context-specific, differentiated). DG INTPA will
also focus on creating conditions for innovative ways of financing to promote economic
inclusion and access to finance for the most vulnerable, including refugees, displaced and
.
In Afghanistan and in Myanmar, DG INTPA will continue delivering basic needs and
livelihoods assistance, targeting women, girls, and vulnerable groups, such as IDPs, returnees,
and host communities. Despite growing restrictions on fundamental rights and context-related
challenges, DG INTPA will build on past successes to promote community-based, private sector-
led recovery and inclusive growth, empowering women to contribute meaningfully. The
response will remain flexible, considering future risks (e.g. increased restrictions in the
operating environment). DG INTPA will also continue enhancing regional cooperation with
(7) DG ECHO: Directorate-General for European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations.
11

neighbouring Central Asian countries for Afghanistan, as well as with South and South-East
Asia countries for Myanmar.
DG INTPA will also step up efforts to deliver on the Women, Peace and Security agenda in a
Team Europe approach, in the aftermath to the 25th anniversary of the Women, Peace and
Security agenda and against the backdrop of increased conflicts, such as in Sudan, and
resulting serious human rights violations, including sexual and gender-based violence.
Accountability work will be pursued, including through the Global Initiative Against Impunity,
operating in 23 countries.
In Haiti, DG INTPA will continue to provide support in critical areas, including strengthening
economic governance, combating illicit trafficking, improving access to essential services as
education, and reducing community-level violence. In addition to the Global Gateway Technical
and Vocational Education and Training Campus, the Multi-sector Program for the Resilience and
Recovery of Social Services will contribute to the stabilisation and recovery of the country. In
Venezuela, DG INTPA is preparing a new intervention to be implemented as from 2026, taking
place in a politically sensitive environment. Building on partnerships with Venezuelan
stakeholders, and coordinated with EU Member States and international partners, the initiative
aims to foster dialogue, democracy, equality, and the rule of law in Venezuela.
The global Team Europe Democracy Initiative will allow the EU and 14 EU Member States
to enhance the impact of evidence-based and joint actions in promoting democratic governance
in partner countries. It will also inform and support the implementation of the Civil Society
strategy and of the Democracy Shield, feeding the newly created EU Centre on Democratic
Resilience with tools and evidence from external democracy support practices. Priorities in 2026
and deliverables on the ground will include supporting local democracy actors, human rights
defenders and independent media, promoting civic engagement of youth and women and
institutional strengthening, notably through support to Parliamentary cooperation. DG INTPA will
provide electoral assistance at the regional level, in a strategic and focussed manner.
Specific objective 6.9: Multilateralism is strengthened and global challenges (8) are
addressed, through cooperation with the UN, international financial institutions
(IFIs), and other partners, leveraging Team Europe for more visibility and impact
At a time when the rules-based global order is under attack, and the effectiveness of
international institutions is being questioned, the EU will work to strengthen effective
multilateralism, including by reforming and streamlining the system (e.g. UN80 effort (9),
OECD/DAC review). The EU will use the multilateral system, strategic dialogues and high-level
gatherings to advance its priorities, starting with the Global Gateway agenda. It will actively
promote the Team Europe approach in multilateral fora while leveraging the financial
contributions of the EU and its Member States to achieve greater policy influence and visibility.
DG INTPA will continue to promote policy objectives, interests and values in global
negotiations relating to sustainable development. The outcomes of key intergovernmental
conferences will be incorporated into work programme.

with climate change, biodiversity and forests.

relevance for a rapidly changing world.

In addressing global challenges, notably the eradication of poverty (10), the financial
contributions of the EU and its Member States to multilateral partners will translate into
greater policy influence and visibility.
DG INTPA, as the lead service within the Commission vis-à-vis the World Bank, will continue to
promote the close coordination of the EU and its Member States (Team Europe approach) with
the IFIs, which together have sizeable financial assistance capacity, so that they collectively use
this potential to promote EU priorities and strategic objectives. In particular, following the
signature of a cooperation arrangement on high-impact projects by Commission President von
der Leyen and World Bank Group (WBG) President Banga, DG INTPA will consolidate the
strategic cooperation launched in 2025 by strengthening coordination at political and technical
levels with the WBG around an initial selection of 18 high-impact projects in partner countries
and enhancing the joint communication of concrete deliverables. Additionally, DG INTPA will
further support the strengthening of the international financial architecture to better
address global and development challenges and will encourage multilateral development banks
to implement the G20 Roadmap, aiming to make them better, bigger and more effective.
DG INTPA will maintain close cooperation with multilateral partners through participation in
high-level multilateral events and dialogues, including fostering the G7 and G20 sustainable
development agendas, and will promote coordination with like-minded partners. DG INTPA leads
; it will make the
partnership more strategic, focussing on strengthening the enabling environment and good
governance to support Global Gateway strategy, and supporting our efforts in fragile contexts.
DG INTPA will be actively involved in discussions on the effectiveness and efficiency of the
global aid architecture, including prioritisation, enhancing country-level ownership and
ensuring complementarities and synergies, notably between different global health and
education initiatives. DG INTPA will maintain its support to global health and education
initiatives, while engaging with like-minded partners to enhance the global education and
health architectures, the latter in the context of the Global Health Resilience Initiative.
DG INTPA will continue to cooperate with EU Member States, partner countries, UN agencies
and IFIs to achieve internationally agreed goals under multilateral environment
agreements (11). Furthermore, DG INTPA will support global actions against wildlife trafficking.
It will also promote nuclear safety via the International Atomic Energy Agency and the G7.
Collaboration with the Committee on World Food Security and the UN Rome-based Agencies (12)
will help tackle the challenges of hunger and malnutrition and to deliver on the commitments
renewed at the Nutrition for Growth summit in 2025.
Furthermore, DG INTPA will continue to contribute to multilateral efforts on human rights,
including through continued support to the UN human rights pillar, notably the Office of the
United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, as well as to global, regional and national
human rights bodies and international jurisdictions, particularly the International Criminal Court.

Key simplification and implementation activities and outputs in 2026
DG INTPA will continue implementing measures (13) contributing to the overarching objective of
making Europe simpler and faster in line with the Communication
faster Europe: Communication on
no regulatory competencies and does not carry out any stress-test plan as it does not establish
any acquis to simplify. However, it interacts with a variety of stakeholders who often play an
essential role in the implementation of projects managed by DG INTPA.
DG INTPA will continue to engage with such stakeholders, in particular civil society, local
authorities, the private sector, European development financial institutions, EU
agencies and administrations. In 2025, two Implementation Dialogues were organised: one with
civil society organisations and local authorities and another with the private sector. In 2026, DG
INTPA intends to convene two Implementation Dialogues (14), as well as other meetings and
consultations such as reality checks. For example, DG INTPA will organise its regular
consultations on the regional multiannual programming with the Policy Forum on Development
(PFD) and on the Global Gateway strategy roll-out with the Global Gateway Civil Society and
Local Authorities Advisory Platform. DG INTPA will continue to focus on translating the main
takeaways of such meetings into further simplification and adaptation of its working methods
to better respond to the needs expressed by the implementing partners and thus facilitate their
work.
procedures (grants and procurement). In the same vein, DG INTPA will continue its open-access
online resources (e.g. courses, templates, guidance) for the benefit of the public.
As an outcome of the 2025 implementation dialogue with CSOs and local authorities, DG INTPA
will support the implementation of the fourth generation of Civil Society Roadmaps in all EU
delegations in order to strengthen early engagement of civil society in the design of Global
Gateway projects in partner countries. Other ongoing engagement mechanisms with CSOs and
local authorities will continue through the Policy Forum on Development in support of
knowledge sharing and peer-to-peer exchanges. Furthermore, to facilitate access to finance for
local authorities and smaller CSOs, DG INTPA will explore increasingly the use of tools such as
finance not linked to costs, financial support to third parties and direct access to finance for
local authorities.

Data protection
DG INTPA will continue the implementation of data protection rules in accordance with the
Commission's Data Protection Action Plan (25) as reviewed in 2020 (26) by ensuring that all staff
is aware of data protection rules and that compliance is documented with data protection legal
framework (27). The timely and proper information to data subjects regarding the processing of
their personal data by DG INTPA via the delivery of privacy statements remains a priority.
In 2025, DG INTPA submitted five new data processing records to the Data Protection Office
(DPO) for review and received feedback. In 2026, DG INTPA aims to publish these records on
the public register of the DPO. In compliance with the bi-annual review policy of data
processing records, DG INTPA will continue to review its already published records accordingly.
In DG INTPA, awareness about data protection is primarily obtained through extensive guidance
available to all staff. DG INTPA will continue to raise awareness in 2026 by guiding new staff
and offering training courses and events to current staff and newcomers to ensure compliance
and maintain a high level of awareness.
C. Sound financial management
The internal control framework supports sound management and decision-making. In particular,
it ensures that risks to the achievement of objectives are addressed and reduced to acceptable
levels through cost-effective controls. DG INTPA has established an internal control system
tailored to its characteristics and circumstances. The effectiveness of this internal control
system will be assessed on an ongoing basis throughout the year and will be object of an
annual assessment covering all internal control principles.
Throughout 2026, DG INTPA will pursue the implementation of its annual action plan which
addresses identified control weaknesses and high risks (28). This action plan continues the
implementation of actions to respond to the recent findings of control processes, such as audits
and verifications. The action plan prioritises actions targeting grants in direct and indirect
management, actions concerning indirect management with international organisations
development agencies, as well as cross-cutting weaknesses and risks. These actions also build
on the weaknesses as identified in the internal control system. In 2026, DG INTPA aims to have
an error rate identified through all relevant control systems below 2%.
For 2026, DG INTPA targets reducing the costs of control to 4% (29). The main components of
these costs are human resources costs which will be closely monitored throughout 2026 even
though this is not under DG INTPA control. Moreover, under the lead of DG BUDG, DG HR and
the Secretariat-General, DG INTPA will contribute to the cost-benefit analysis for the direct
programme implementation 2028-2034.

In May 2025, DG INTPA launched the revision of its anti-fraud strategy (AFS) for the 2025-
2028 period, incorporating Commission anti-fraud priorities, changes brought by the new
Financial Regulation and, the objectives of -Fraud Strategy (CAFS) Action

implementation of the Global Gateway strategy
and effective amid new geopolitical landscape.
In 2026, DG INTPA will continue to monitor the implementation of the activities entrusted to it
under the CAFS and its corresponding Action Plan. This will be done through its dedicated
working group, with a focus on: i) joint ethics and anti-fraud training (30); ii) awareness raising
of pillar-assessed partners on their obligation to notify the Commission of cases of detected
irregularities, fraud and exclusion situations (31); and iii) actions to reduce the risks associated
with local agents in EU delegations (32). Additionally, efforts will be made to strengthen digital
control of external service providers and experts (33). In line with the priorities, DG INTPA
will maintain close collaboration and coordination with the European Anti-Fraud Office, the
European Public Prosecutor's Office, the EEAS, and other Directorates-General within the RELEX
family (16) in the fight against fraud in EU external action. This coordinated approach will enable
DG INTPA to effectively implement its own anti-fraud strategy, leveraging synergies and
expertise to combat fraud and ensure the integrity of EU funds in its operations.
